reference_items.figure_description:
A grid of 9 columns and 5 rows of 1 cm by 1 cm squares containing a shaded polygon. Outside the bottom-right corner of the grid, dimension arrows indicate that a single square is 1 cm wide and 1 cm high.

Defining grid coordinates from the top-left corner (0, 0) to the bottom-right corner (9, 5):
- The shaded polygon has vertices at (3, 1), (5, 1), (6, 2), (5, 3), (5, 4), and (3, 4).
- The left side is a vertical line from (3, 1) down to (3, 4), spanning 3 units.
- The bottom side runs horizontally from (3, 4) to (5, 4), spanning 2 units.
- The right side goes vertically up from (5, 4) to (5, 3), 1 unit.
- From (5, 3), a diagonal side goes up and to the right to grid intersection (6, 2).
- From (6, 2), a diagonal side goes up and to the left to grid intersection (5, 1).
- The top side runs horizontally from (5, 1) left to (3, 1), spanning 2 units.

reference_items.figure_description:
Five identical squares, labeled A through E, each partitioned and shaded differently:
- Option A: The square is divided horizontally into 5 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded grey and the bottom 3 strips are unshaded (white).
- Option B: The square is divided by a diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, and a line segment from the center to the bottom-right corner. The entire upper-left triangular half is shaded grey, the right triangular section is shaded grey, and the bottom triangular section is unshaded.
- Option C: The square is divided by two vertical lines into three strips: a narrow shaded strip on the left, a wide unshaded strip in the middle, and a narrow shaded strip on the right.
- Option D: An unshaded triangle has its base along the entire bottom edge of the square and its apex at the midpoint of the top edge. The two right triangles flanking it on the left and right are shaded grey.
- Option E: The square is divided by two vertical lines into 3 equal-width vertical strips. The left strip and the right strip are shaded grey, and the middle strip is unshaded.

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by squares and a cube to the right of the pattern]

options.label: B

options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by square and two triangles coming out of two sides of the square and a square base pyramid to the right of the pattern]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: a pattern made up by two large rectangles and four small rectangles with two of the smaller rectangles coming out of the opposite shorter sides of the large rectangles and a rectangular prism]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four multiple-choice options, each showing a 2D net (with dashed interior fold lines) beside a 3D container (with dashed hidden edges):
- Option A: A net of 5 congruent squares arranged in an inverted U-shape (a row of 3 squares across the top, and 1 square hanging down from each of the left and right squares, leaving the middle space empty). Beside it is a line drawing of a cube.
- Option B: A net consisting of a horizontal rectangle with a circle attached to each of its two shorter vertical ends. Beside it is a line drawing of a vertical cylinder.
- Option C: A net consisting of a square with two triangles attached to adjacent sides: one extending down from the bottom side and one extending to the right from the right side. Beside it is a line drawing of an inverted square-based pyramid pointing downward.
- Option D: A net consisting of a horizontal row of four rectangles alternating in width (narrow, wide, narrow, wide), with a narrow rectangle attached to the top of the first wide rectangle and a narrow rectangle attached to the bottom of the second wide rectangle. Beside it is a line drawing of a matching upright rectangular prism.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three figures made of matches arranged in a horizontal row, labeled below with numbers 1, 2, and 3:
- Figure 1: 4 matches arranged to form a single square (one match on each of the four sides).
- Figure 2: 7 matches arranged to form a row of two attached squares side by side, sharing one vertical match in the middle (2 top, 2 bottom, and 3 vertical matches).
- Figure 3: 10 matches arranged to form a row of three attached squares side by side, each adjacent pair sharing a vertical match (3 top, 3 bottom, and 4 vertical matches).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
